For example, by changing the use of existing rooms, removing or replacing unsightly features, clearing obstacles to easy circulation, rearranging direction signs and generally introducing as much order as possible, most outdated station buildings can be made reasonably efficient and attractive.

glosses: Out of date; not the latest; obsolete.

examples.text: Your version of the document is outdated.

glosses: Too old to be used; not current; invalid; having expired.

examples.text: My bus pass is out of date — I'll have to go buy a new one.
I can't eat this salad, it's out of date.
Owing to the time lag which must occur between the dates of closing for press and publication, it sometimes happens that items of news are out of date, or inaccurate, by the time they reach readers.

glosses: Not conforming to the current fashion or style; old-fashioned; outmoded.

examples.text: The dresses she wears are quite out of date.

glosses: Alternative form of out of date.

examples.text: The Rabbit could not claim to be a model of anything, for he didn’t know that real rabbits existed; he thought they were all stuffed with sawdust like himself, and he understood that sawdust was quite out-of-date and should never be mentioned in modern circles.
This new yard will replace a group of out-of-date yards, and there will be an estimated net saving of £150,000 a year.
